claims.claim: For m,n≥2, the sortable component has Q=(mn)! states if m or n is even and Q=(mn)!/2 states if both are odd.
claims.evidence: Source Remark 1 states that a configuration is sortable exactly when at least one of m, n, or its permutation is even. Thus all (mn)! permutations occur if a dimension is even, while precisely the alternating half occurs when both dimensions are odd.
claims.witness: The checker found 720 reachable states on 2×3 and 181440=9!/2 on 3×3.
claims.search_method: Direct deduction from the source's sortable-instance characterization, followed by exhaustive small-board BFS.

claims.claim: On a p×q board where pushes in both directions are allowed, an involution π on any chosen row can be applied in at most 3q+3a₂(π) pushes, with the only side effect being a one-step cyclic shift, in a chosen direction, of the body of each of a₂(π) fixed auxiliary columns.
claims.evidence: The source's three-scan SwapPairs trace uses q row pushes per scan and one forward or inverse rotation of each auxiliary column. In the bidirectional model, every block of p−1 forward rotations implementing an inverse is exactly one reverse push. The source trace therefore remains unchanged and costs exactly 3q+3a₂(π).
claims.witness: Independent simulation passed 27760 cases with 2≤p≤6, 2≤q≤7, every chosen row, all partial matchings, both shift directions, and multiple auxiliary-column choices.
claims.search_method: Re-derived the three scans from the source and simulated their exact position permutations.

claims.claim: Every even permutation is a product συ of two involutions with a₂(σ)=a₂(υ); every odd permutation is a product συτ where τ is a transposition and a₂(σ)=a₂(υ).
claims.evidence: The source's cycle-reflection proof is complete: odd-length cycles give balanced factors, and the two possible factorizations of each even-length cycle have opposite unit imbalances. Pairing those imbalances proves the even case; removing one transposition from the remaining imbalance proves the odd case.
claims.witness: Exhaustive enumeration verified both assertions for every permutation on up to seven elements.
claims.search_method: Checked the source's cycle-by-cycle construction and independently enumerated all balanced-involution products.

claims.claim: For adjacent rows r,r+1 and adjacent columns c,c+1, the eight-push word R_r^{-1}C_c^{-1}R_rC_cC_{c+1}R_{r+1}C_{c+1}^{-1}R_{r+1}^{-1} swaps the two positions in columns c,c+1 in each of those two rows and fixes every other position; its transpose gives the analogous pair of vertical swaps.
claims.evidence: Direct position tracking gives exactly two disjoint horizontal transpositions and no other movement. Transposing rows and columns preserves the word identity and gives the vertical version.
claims.witness: The exact checker verified all 784 choices of dimensions 2 through 8 and all non-wrapping adjacent row/column pairs, including every two-cell degeneracy.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive exact permutation evaluation of the stated eight pushes.

claims.claim: On any m×n board with m,n≥2, every globally even permutation that preserves each row setwise, or preserves each column setwise, can be performed exactly in O(mn) bidirectional pushes.
claims.evidence: Each even permutation on a length-ℓ line costs at most 9ℓ via two balanced involutions with opposite body shifts. For odd line permutations, splitting off one fixed adjacent transposition leaves an even factor. Global evenness makes the number of residual transpositions even, and the path-incidence construction using Claim 3 realizes exactly that subset in at most 8(k−1) pushes. Hence the total is at most 9kℓ+8(k−1)=O(mn).
claims.witness: The local involution and double-swap primitives, including length-two lines, were independently checked exactly.
claims.search_method: Symbolic parity decomposition and path-incidence proof, supported by exact primitive checks.

claims.claim: Every permutation P of the mn cells admits a three-layer factorization P=C₂RC₁, where C₁ and C₂ preserve every column setwise and R preserves every row setwise.
claims.evidence: The source-column/destination-column multigraph is m-regular on both sides. For every left vertex set X, its m|X| incident edges fit only in vertices N(X), whose total degree is m|N(X)|, proving Hall's condition. Repeated removal of perfect matchings yields m colors. Routing color into an intermediate row, then destination column, then destination row gives the claimed column-row-column factorization.
claims.witness: The m perfect-matching colors assign every source-column token and every destination column exactly once in each intermediate row.
claims.search_method: Independent Hall-theorem and edge-coloring derivation.

claims.claim: Every even permutation of an m×n board with m,n≥2 is realizable in O(mn) bidirectional pushes.
claims.evidence: In a three-layer factorization of an even P, either zero or two layers are odd. Multiplying each odd layer by a line-supported transposition produces realizable even layers E_i. The displayed expansion of E^{-1}P is valid and leaves a product of zero or two transpositions: identity, one 3-cycle, or two disjoint transpositions. The latter is a product of two 3-cycles. The source supplies arbitrary 3-cycles with constantly many compound rotations, hence O(max{m,n})=O(mn) unit pushes. Three O(mn) corrected layers plus this residual prove the claim.
claims.witness: The residual classification exhausts equal, one-point-overlapping, and disjoint pairs of transpositions.
claims.search_method: Checked the layer-parity algebra, conjugation types, and transfer from compound rotations to bidirectional unit pushes.

claims.claim: Every sortable m×n configuration with m,n≥2 can be sorted in O(mn) bidirectional pushes.
claims.evidence: Claim 6 handles every even sorting permutation. An odd sortable permutation requires an even line length; one unit rotation of such a line is odd, so composing it with the desired permutation leaves an even residual handled by Claim 6. Odd-by-odd sortable configurations are already even by the source characterization.
claims.witness: The parity of a unit rotation of a length-k line is (−1)^(k−1), so it is odd exactly when k is even.
claims.search_method: Complete case split over configuration parity and the two dimension parities.

claims.claim: If min{m,n}=1 and N=mn, then D(m,n)=floor(N/2).
claims.evidence: With one dimension equal to one, all nonidentity moves generate the same cyclic rotation group. The sortable component therefore consists of the N cyclic shifts, and shift a has word distance min(a mod N,N−(a mod N)). Its maximum is floor(N/2), including zero for N=1.
claims.witness: The antipodal cyclic shift attains floor(N/2).
claims.search_method: Direct Cayley-graph analysis of the one-generator cyclic component.

claims.claim: Every instance A has the displacement certificate pn(A)≥ceil(H(A)/n)+ceil(V(A)/m). Moreover, a global translation by a columns and b rows has exact push number m·d_n(a)+n·d_m(b), where d_k(z)=min(z mod k,k−(z mod k)).
claims.evidence: A row push changes the sum of cyclic horizontal distances by at most n and leaves vertical distances unchanged; the symmetric statement holds for a column push. The required row- and column-push lower bounds therefore add. For a global translation, H=mn·d_n(a) and V=mn·d_m(b), and independently rotating all rows and columns along shortest directions attains the lower bound.
claims.witness: The checker confirmed the certificate against every reachable state on 2×2, 2×3, and 3×3 and confirmed every 2×3 translation distance exactly.
claims.search_method: Lipschitz-potential proof plus exhaustive small-board distance comparison.

claims.claim: The maximum possible value of the displacement certificate is exactly m·floor(n/2)+n·floor(m/2), which is at most N=mn; a half-translation attains it.
claims.evidence: Each of the N tokens contributes at most floor(n/2) horizontally and floor(m/2) vertically. Taking ceilings after division yields the stated upper bound, and each summand is at most N/2. Translating by floor(n/2) columns and floor(m/2) rows makes every token attain both pointwise maxima, so equality holds.
claims.witness: The exhaustive maxima are 4, 5, and 6 on 2×2, 2×3, and 3×3 respectively, matching the formula.
claims.search_method: Pointwise extremal-distance argument and exhaustive small-board verification.

claims.claim: For arbitrary p,q≥2, FillColumns makes every column near-full using O(pq log q) pushes; the proof does not require p≤q.
claims.evidence: The source's proof of the FillColumns subroutine uses no comparison between the dimensions. Each column rotates at most p−1 times. If f columns remain underfull, a complete q-push row scan reduces the wrong-body-token potential by at least f/2. In a dyadic phase the potential is below (p−1)q/2^{i−1}, so fewer than 4p complete scans occur. Summing O(log q) phases gives O(pq log q) row pushes and O(pq) column pushes.
claims.witness: The dimension assumption p≤q appears in the source's surrounding full algorithm, not in any inequality used by the FillColumns potential proof.
claims.search_method: Line-by-line dependency audit of the source's FillColumns lemmas.

claims.claim: For arbitrary p,q≥2, FloatMinimums transforms a matrix whose columns are all near-full into one whose columns are all body-full using O(pq) pushes.
claims.evidence: Near-fullness leaves exactly one representative of each target column in the buffer row. A q-step sweep aligns each representative with its target column. At that moment the whole column has the correct target-column label, and at most p−1 column pushes place its unique target-buffer token at the head. No dimension-order assumption is used, and the total is q+q(p−1)=pq.
claims.witness: Each column is finalized once and never rotated again by the procedure.
claims.search_method: Invariant and operation-count audit of FloatMinimums.

claims.claim: Given a p×q matrix in which every column is body-full, its buffer row can be sorted in O(q) bidirectional pushes while preserving the set of tokens in every column body.
claims.evidence: For an even buffer permutation, Claim 2 supplies two involutions with equal transposition counts, and opposite-direction applications from Claim 1 cancel all body shifts. In the odd case, the same construction leaves one transposition; applying it causes only one cyclic body shift, which preserves that body's token set. Since every involution has at most q/2 transpositions, the cost is O(q), independent of p.
claims.witness: The exact SwapPairs checks include even and odd buffer permutations through their disjoint transposition sets.
claims.search_method: Composed the verified involution factorization with the verified bidirectional SwapPairs trace.

claims.claim: For arbitrary m,n≥2 and N=mn, any m×n configuration can be transformed in O(N log m) pushes into one in which every row contains exactly its target-row token set. In particular, this costs O(N log min{m,n}) when m≤n.
claims.evidence: After transposition the dimensions are p=n,q=m. Claims 11–13 make every transposed column contain exactly its target-column set in O(pq log q)+O(pq)+O(q)=O(N log m) pushes. Transposing back converts precisely that property into correct target-row membership. When m≤n, m=min{m,n}.
claims.witness: The coordinate map sends an original target row to a transposed target column without changing the number of pushes.
claims.search_method: Coordinate-by-coordinate transpose audit and composition of Claims 11–13.

claims.claim: The parent's short-dimension reorientation does not justify its former row-specific O(N log min{m,n}) conclusion on a fixed tall labeling.
claims.evidence: On a fixed tall labeling, transposing to make the shorter dimension the row dimension converts oriented-row membership back into original-column membership, not original-row membership. Those properties are inequivalent, so the cited transpose-back inference cannot establish the former row-specific conclusion.
claims.witness: For ((1,2),(3,5),(4,6)), the stated output ((1,2),(5,4),(3,6)) has target column sets {1,3,5} and {2,4,6}, but rows {4,5} and {3,6} are not the target sets {3,4} and {5,6}.
claims.search_method: Explicit coordinate-objective comparison and direct set calculation on the supplied 3×2 example.

claims.claim: Assume 2≤m≤n and every row of a sortable m×n board already contains exactly its target-row token set. The board can then be sorted in O(mn) bidirectional pushes.
claims.evidence: Even row corrections cost O(n) with canceled side effects. If n is even, one odd row push changes an odd correction to even. If n is odd and m even, the residual transposition leaves an (m−1)-cycle on one column body; this cycle is even and can be undone in O(m). If both dimensions are odd, global sortability makes the number of odd row corrections even, and Claim 3 batches their common residual transposition. Summed over m rows, the cost is O(m(n+m))=O(mn) because m≤n.
claims.witness: The dimension/parity cases (n even), (n odd,m even), and (m,n both odd) exhaust all possibilities.
claims.search_method: Full dimension-parity case analysis using Claims 1–4.

claims.claim: Let D(m,n) be the maximum push number of a sortable m×n instance, N=mn, and s=min{m,n}. The earlier constructive route gives D(m,n)=O(N·max{1,log s}), and in particular O(N log s) for m,n≥2.
claims.evidence: Orienting the entire puzzle as an s×max{m,n} instance is valid because both the initial and target coordinates are transposed together. Claim 14 obtains target-row membership in O(N log s), and Claim 16 finishes in O(N). Claim 8 supplies the s=1 case.
claims.witness: Unlike Claim 15's fixed-label intermediate assertion, this argument transposes the entire sorting objective and therefore maps a sorted output back to a sorted output.
claims.search_method: Dependency and transpose-scope audit of Claims 8, 14, and 16.

claims.claim: For all m,n≥2, every configuration, including a nonsortable odd configuration on an odd-by-odd board, can be transformed in O(mn) pushes into one with correct target-row token sets.
claims.evidence: Every configuration is sortable when a dimension is even, and every even configuration is sortable on an odd-by-odd board, so Claim 7 handles those cases. For an odd odd-by-odd configuration A, choose the sorted board B with two tokens in one row transposed. B is odd and row-correct, making the relative permutation from A to B even; Claim 6 realizes it in O(mn).
claims.witness: The row-internal transposition defining B preserves every target-row token set while changing global parity.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive parity case split and relative-permutation argument.

claims.claim: For every fixed s≥2, boards with min{m,n}=s have asymptotically tight push number D(m,n)=Θ(mn).
claims.evidence: For fixed s, Claim 17's O(N log s) is O(N). The half-translation lower bound includes max{m,n}·floor(s/2), which is a positive constant fraction of N for every fixed s≥2. Thus upper and lower bounds are both linear.
claims.witness: If m=s≤n, then n·floor(s/2)=(floor(s/2)/s)N.
claims.search_method: Specialized the established upper bound and exact translation lower bound to fixed s.

claims.claim: For m,n≥2, a counting lower bound is D(m,n)≥ceil(log_{d−1}(1+(d−2)(Q−1)/d)), where d=2(m+n), Q=(mn)! if m or n is even, and Q=(mn)!/2 otherwise.
claims.evidence: A geodesic has no generator immediately followed by its inverse, so the number of formal words of length at most L is bounded by 1+d((d−1)^L−1)/(d−2). Duplicate directions on two-cell lines only increase this upper count. A radius-D ball contains all Q component states from Claim 0; rearranging the inequality and using integrality gives exactly the displayed ceiling.
claims.witness: The exact formula evaluates to 2 on 2×2 and 5 on 3×3.
claims.search_method: Independent reduced-word counting derivation with exact-integer evaluation.

claims.claim: For m,n≥2, the numerical counting certificate above is always at most 2N, so this reduced-word obstruction cannot establish a superlinear lower bound.
claims.evidence: Writing X=1+(d−2)(Q−1)/d gives X<Q≤N!<N^N. Also d−1=2(m+n)−1>sqrt(N) for m,n≥2, hence log_{d−1}N<2 and log_{d−1}X<2N. Since 2N is integral, the ceiling is at most 2N. This uniformly limits this particular certificate to a linear value.
claims.witness: Exact-integer evaluation confirmed the inequality for every 2≤m,n≤100 without floating-point arithmetic.
claims.search_method: General analytic inequality plus exact finite-range stress test.

claims.claim: Global translations are not generally diametral: D(2,3)=7, whereas every translated 2×3 board has distance at most 5.
claims.evidence: Independent BFS with the seven distinct 2×3 generators reached all 720 configurations with levels [1,7,31,115,274,253,36,3], proving diameter 7. The exact translation formula has maximum 2·floor(3/2)+3·floor(2/2)=5.
claims.witness: The stated seven-push word reaches ((3,2,1),(6,5,4)), and the independent BFS assigns that state distance 7.
claims.search_method: Complete exact BFS and exhaustive enumeration of all six global translations.

claims.claim: Exact square boundary cases give D(2,2)=4 and D(3,3)=8; on 3×3 the maximum displacement certificate is 6 and the corrected two-dimensional counting certificate is 5.
claims.evidence: Independent complete BFS gives levels [1,4,10,8,1] on the 24-state 2×2 component and [1,12,96,736,5208,28674,89497,54741,2475] on the 181440-state 3×3 component, so the diameters are 4 and 8. Exhaustive displacement evaluation gives maximum 6 on 3×3, and exact-integer substitution in Claim 20 gives 5.
claims.witness: The BFS state counts equal 4! and 9!/2 respectively, with last nonempty levels 4 and 8.
claims.search_method: Complete exact BFS, exhaustive displacement calculation, and exact counting-formula evaluation.

claims.claim: Let N=mn. Uniformly for m,n≥2, D(m,n)=Θ(N); together with D(1,N)=D(N,1)=floor(N/2), this closes the source's multiplicative logarithmic gap at the requested asymptotic strength.
claims.evidence: Claims 4–7 give a uniform O(N) construction for every sortable two-dimensional instance. Claims 9–10 give a sortable half-translation of exact distance m·floor(n/2)+n·floor(m/2), which is at least 2N/3 because floor(k/2)≥k/3 for k≥2. Claim 8 handles the one-dimensional component exactly. Thus the upper and lower bounds match linearly in every regime and the logarithmic gap is closed.
claims.witness: For every m,n≥2, 2N/3≤D(m,n)≤cN for a dimension-independent construction constant c.
claims.search_method: End-to-end dependency audit of the structural upper bound and explicit translation lower bound.

target_evidence: The draft supplies a complete uniform linear upper bound: Hall decomposition factors any position permutation into three line-preserving layers; globally even layers are realized in O(N) using balanced involutions and the exact double-swap primitive; parity correction leaves at most two transpositions, handled by at most two source-supported arbitrary 3-cycles. One odd line push reduces every remaining sortable odd case to the even case. The independently verified displacement argument supplies a sortable half-translation at distance at least 2N/3, while the one-dimensional diameter is floor(N/2). Therefore D(m,n)=Θ(mn) at the requested strength, with no uncovered dimension or parity case.
